cards.text: In those days, there was no king in Israel. A Levite living way out in the remote hill country of Ephraim takes a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah. Friend, I'll be straight with you: this is one of the hardest stories in the whole Bible, so stay close to me on this one.

cards.question: The Levite's concubine is unfaithful to him and leaves him. Whose house in Bethlehem does she go back to?

cards.text: She's been there four months. Then her husband gets up and goes after her, taking his servant and a pair of donkeys.

cards.question: The Levite travels all the way to Bethlehem after his concubine. What does he go there to do?

answers.text: Speak kindly to her and bring her back
Bring her before the town elders

cards.question: The girl brings the Levite into her father's house. True or false: her father is unhappy to see him.

cards.text: Her father gladly welcomes him and persuades him to stay. So the Levite stays three days, eating, drinking and lodging there.

cards.question: On the fourth day, the Levite is up early and ready to leave. What does the girl's father tell him first?

answers.text: Have a bite of bread before you go
The roads are too dangerous today
My daughter is not ready to leave

cards.text: So the two of them sit down and eat and drink together. Then the father asks him to stay the night, and when the man gets up to go, his father-in-law talks him into it.

cards.question: On the fifth day, the Levite gets up early to leave. True or false: he's on the road by morning.

cards.text: They wait until late afternoon and eat again. Then, as the man gets up to leave, the father says the day's almost over, so please spend the night.

cards.question: The father-in-law begs the Levite to spend the night one more time. What does the Levite do?

answers.text: Asks to stay a whole week

cards.text: Off they go with the two saddled donkeys. They come near Jebus, that's Jerusalem, and the day is almost gone.

cards.question: It's getting dark near Jebus. What does the Levite's servant suggest?

answers.text: Stop and spend the night in Jebus
Turn back to the house in Bethlehem
Keep walking all through the night

cards.question: The Levite says no to stopping in Jebus. He won't turn aside to the city of ___.

cards.text: They push on, hoping to reach Gibeah or Ramah, and the sun sets as they near Gibeah in Benjamin. They turn in to lodge there, and the Levite sits down in the city square.

cards.question: The Levite is sitting in Gibeah's city square as night falls. True or false: no one in Gibeah takes them into his home for the night.

cards.text: That evening, an old man comes in from his work in the field. He's from the hill country of Ephraim too, living here in Gibeah, where the men are Benjamites.

cards.question: The old man looks up and sees the traveler in the city square. What does he ask him?

answers.text: Where he is going and where he came from
Whether he can pay for a room tonight
Why he brought his donkeys into town

cards.text: The Levite tells him they're traveling from Bethlehem in Judah to the remote hill country of Ephraim, where he's from.

cards.question: Besides heading home, the Levite tells the old man about one more place he's going. Where is it?

cards.text: He says no one has taken him in, even though they've got straw and feed for the donkeys and bread and wine for themselves. Friend, the man brought his OWN everything, and STILL nobody opens a door.

cards.question: The old man says, "Peace to you," to the Levite in Gibeah. What does he offer him?

answers.text: To sell him food for the road
To guide him on to Ramah

cards.text: Just don't spend the night in the square, the old man says. So he brings them home and feeds the donkeys, and they wash their feet and eat and drink.

But while they're enjoying themselves, the wicked men of the city suddenly surround the house. Pounding on the door, they tell the old man, "Bring out the man who came to your house, so we can have relations with him!"

cards.question: The old man goes out and tells the wicked men of Gibeah, "No, my brothers, do not do this wicked thing!" What reason does he give them?

answers.text: This man is a guest in my house
This man is a priest of the LORD
This man has done nothing wrong

cards.text: Then the old man says, "Look, let me bring out my virgin daughter and the man's concubine, and you can use them and do with them as you wish. But do not do such a vile thing to this man."

cards.question: The old man makes his offer to the wicked men at the door. True or false: they listen to him.

cards.text: So the Levite takes his concubine and sends her outside to them. They rape her and abuse her throughout the night.

cards.question: True or false: at dawn, when the men let her go, the concubine goes back to the house where her master is staying.

cards.text: She collapses at the doorway and lies there until it's light. My heart breaks for her, friend.

cards.question: In the morning, the Levite opens the doors to go out on his journey. There's his concubine, collapsed in the doorway with her hands on the threshold. What does he say to her?

answers.text: Get up and let us go
Forgive me for what I did
Wait here while I find help

cards.text: But there's no response, so he puts her on his donkey and sets out for home. When he gets there, he takes a knife and cuts her limb by limb into twelve pieces.

cards.question: The Levite sends out the twelve pieces. Where does he send them?
Everyone who sees the pieces the Levite sent says nothing like this has been seen or done since the day the Israelites came out of ___.
True or false: everyone who sees the pieces the Levite sent says to keep quiet about it.

cards.text: We'll leave it right here for now, friend. This story isn't over yet.
